we have developed a lossless compression technique, C4, that exceeds the compression efficiency (under limited decoder buffer size) of all other existing algorithms including BZIP2 and 2D-LT, and that we have developed two variations of the encoder, Block C4 and Golomb Context Copy code (GC3), that significantly reduce the encoding complexity, and the Block GC3 decoder that significantly reduces the power and area of the maskless lithography writer chip.

Block C4 and C4 are the most efficient lossless compression algorithms, Block GC3 has the lowest hardware cost of any lossless compression algorithm for the data stream generated by direct-write maskless systems, and that C4 is the most efficient lossy compression algorithm.

In summary, our research is concerned with
developing novel lossless image data compression algorithms for maskless lithographic applications.
developing the most efficient compression algorithms and the most efficient hardware implementations of the compression algorithms for maskless lithographic systems.
developing a high throughput maskless lithography writer system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Block GC3 has a better hardware performance as compared to Block GC3 and Block C4.
Block GC3 is the most promising of the three algorithms in terms of throughput, compression, and complexity.
the Block GC3 algorithm is an excellent candidate to be implemented as the writer chip for direct write maskless lithography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the C4 and GC3 algorithms are the most efficient lossless compression algorithms to date for maskless lithographic data.
we developed two novel compression techniques, C4 and Block C4, that are superior to all other existing techniques, including the state of the art BZIP2, under limited decoder buffer constraints.

we have developed a lossless compression technique that is specifically tailored to flattened data, which exceeds the efficiency of all other techniques, and can be implemented in hardware with low power, small area, and high throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C4 algorithm is a promising candidate for the data compression algorithm for maskless lithographic systems.
the compression ratio and throughput of maskless lithography can be improved significantly by using a combination of C4 and Golomb run-length encoding.
the compression algorithms for direct write maskless lithography should be tailored to the specific application, rather than using the general-purpose compression algorithms.
